scores.notes: This is the strongest engineering spec. The world is a pure, tick-based step function (enterMap/move/interact/tick/commit) with an ordered event list, and roamers use their own RNG stream (roam:seed:map:visits), so chase, flee, ambush and first strike can all be tested in node without touching rngState. It gives a concrete tile legend and map format, and it treats locks, gates and darkness as entities. Each M2 node gets a v1:<id> anchor with a walkability test, and a reachability test walks CRITICAL_PATH with only the keys guaranteed at each point. Its claims check out against the code: temper feeds enchant as floor(temper/2) at stats.js:60; the prologue calls Tamsin 'her' (newgame.js:292); the lore map has 17 markers. It is also the only design that keeps core/save.js free of game logic, by passing the migration in. Its fixture plan is excellent: freeze 18 real saves from the current M2 code before anything is edited. As a player, though, it feels thinner. Three of the 12 new relics are quest gifts instead of being pried from a holder. It skips the lore's feral druids and the Fawnrest pilgrims and miracle-seller. Briarmaw becomes `once`, so there is no Echo rematch. Rabble keep +6 levels per Waking, so after Brand 1 the 'weak foes flee' decision mostly disappears. Instant win gives full XP. It has 13 maps and a sensible cut list. WP-B is overloaded: flow, battle, loot, foe, party, save, migrate, story, tuning and sim all sit with one package.

This has the richest world and follows the lore closely. It includes the feral druids at the Grove-Heart, Vesper the miracle-seller among the pilgrims, smugglers on hidden trails, and the missing patrol turned Hollowed Rangers with Pip's sister Corra and the 'Remember' mechanic. The Reliquary is walkable with lit pedestals, Unsmith letters arrive, Hilda reads the Harrow mark on the mask, and you choose to return or keep the First Seed. Poacher's Holm is visible early at L10. Crownwalls fall when Briarmaw dies. Grudge packs stalk the route. Almost every new relic has a named holder, which is best for the pry-it-loose fantasy. The migration is solid. B alone adds the aethermoor.v1.migrated marker, so 'Start over' cannot bring the M2 save back, plus a 'Restore my M2 save' button. The problem is scope: 21 maps, about 12k tiles, a script VM whose resume state survives a battle and a reload, a Tally-Wagon on a day%3 schedule, dream fights, real-time dt-based pack AI, Stillness, Longwatch and Mercy's Road. That is too much for 8 agents who cannot run git. Checked against the code: B says temper is ceil(temper/2) but the code uses floor. Tamsin is 'he/his' in the boss section, which contradicts the shipped prologue. Running migrate inside core/save.js breaks the core layering. The cold-hearth Domain key (Attunement 2) is trivially met. Rabble still gain +6 per Waking, so fleeing rarely shows after Brand 1. Named holders are variants of rabble families, but escalateSpawn reads FOES[family].tier, not the variant's tier.

This is the design a JRPG fan will love, built on B's lore-faithful world trimmed to 14 maps. It serves the player's own priorities directly. A 'showoff' plays when a hero's gear changes, so you watch them wear the new piece. Tempering visibly brightens the metal, and C changes temper to +1 enchant per step so every step changes a number on the card. Holding on a glinting holder opens its greyed card and stamps it Sighted, exactly as the brief describes. Blocks and lairs show a pre-fight card rated Easy, Fair, Hard or Deadly, so you never blunder into a boss. A Rout pays full gold, 50% XP and a spoils strip whose items open their cards. NPC lines react to the gear you wear. C also sets rabble to +2 levels per Waking instead of +6, which matches the brief's 'rabble never level up' and is the only way the flee-and-Rout decision survives past Brand 1 and into Act II. The save plan is careful. Nothing is written until you move. A carry-over card explains what happened to the old save. A .bak copy is kept before New Game or an import. An e2e test checks that pasting an AETH1 code leaves the .v1 key byte-identical. The cut list names what must never be cut, and the phone controls are specified in detail. The code backs its claims: the stats.js:60, items.js:31 and newgame.js:292 references are right, and battle/party.js lays out ids.length columns, so the one-hero Tamsin duel is less risky than C fears. Weak spots: WP4 is overloaded. A p95 frame gate under 8 ms will flake in headless CI. The Atlas image may take up to 240 KB. The Mire Pearl sits in a chest instead of in a holder's hands. Scaling heroForge by 0.5 touches the battle hero rig the player already approved. The carry-over card's example says 'you wake at the Milestone Fire', but the rule puts looped saves in the Hall.

best_ideas_to_graft: From A: replace C's dt-based stepPack with A's pure tick-based world engine in rules/world.js. The shape is Walk = {map, x, y, face, t, roamers, pending} with enterMap/move/interact/tick/commit and an ordered event list (step, bump, exit, sealed, encounter, contact{ambush, firstStrike}, instant-win, talk, chest, lock, hearthfire, sighted). Roamers run on their own RNG stream, createRng('roam:'+seed+':'+map+':'+visits), and never touch rngState. Keep C's feel on top of it: the '!' freeze beat, chase speed, packs that never enter doors or 1-tile corridors, and tap-to-walk through findPath.

From A: pass the migration into the save module: loadGame(migrate) and importCode(code, migrate), called from ui/app.js and settings.js. core/save.js must not import rules/ (ARCHITECTURE.md layering). Keep migrate pure and idempotent, fill in missing fields on v2 saves, and keep the old node as C's progress.m2 = {node, lastHearthfire}.

From A: before any M2 file is edited, generate the fixtures from the current code with tools/make-v1-fixtures.mjs. That means one save at each of the 14 nodes, one after the Brand, one at Waking 2 with a duplicate 'brand-of-briars' (M2's earnBrand pushes the Brand on every Briarmaw win), one with live grudges and one with a shattered Thornsplitter. Test on every fixture that seed, rngState, party, inventory, bag, gold, codex, waking, brands, cleared, done, grudges, day and runs stay deep-equal.

From A: put a v1:<m2-node-id> anchor on the maps, with a test that every anchor is walkable. Add a reachability test that walks CRITICAL_PATH with only the keys guaranteed at each point, and a test that every lock has both a relic key and a Domain key.

From B: set an aethermoor.v1.migrated marker so 'Start over' in M3 never brings the M2 save back. Add a Settings button 'Restore my M2 save / Export M2 backup (AETH1)' that reads the untouched v1 key. Combine this with C's .v2.bak copy and write-nothing-until-you-move.

From A: add a REGIONS table in data/world.js with act, lore centre, entry exits and Brand ids, so the Hearth Clock already reads 'Brands x/8' and M4 opens Sunscorch by swapping `sealed` for `open`, as data only. Also add A's two extra sealed exits: the Fen Stair out of Mossfall (Gloomfen) and the Highfold Path out of Fawnrest (Ironspire).

From A: build the 16x24 walker as a separate rig in art/walkers.js, fed by the same gearLooks(heroGear) output as the battle sprite, instead of adding scale:.5/back:true to heroForge. The battle, party and card screens share heroForge and the player already approved that art. If heroForge scaling is kept, require a gallery snapshot diff of the battle heroes.
From A: gate performance at p95 frame under 16 ms at 4x CPU throttling, at most 30 drawImage calls per frame, a loop that allocates nothing, and 10 to 15 fps when idle. C's 8 ms e2e gate will flake.

From B: Grudge-bearing encounters get a wider leash and 'stalk the route' with a red title plate. Send an Unsmith letter after each Brand. Hilda reads the maker's mark on the Ichor Mask (the Harrow hook). Give the Mire Pearl to a named holder (B's Gorrow the Mire-King) instead of a shrine chest, so every legend has a holder.

Fix required for C's rabble change: escalateSpawn (rules/foe.js) reads FOES[spawn.family].tier. It must use familyOf(spawn).tier, so relic-bearer variants of rabble families (Mags the smuggler queen, Hollis, Gorrow) still gain +6 levels and their Omens. A pack that holds or wears an unclaimed relic must never flee or be Routed.

Count Brands as a Set wherever they are counted (Hearth Clock, act1-complete, the to-be-continued card) and keep the saved array byte-for-byte, because M2 saves can hold duplicate brand-of-briars. Add a sim mode for a migrated Waking-2 save meeting the new content at +12 levels.
fatal_flaws: A and B: rabble keep TUNING.waking.levels = 6 per Waking. After Brand 1 the Hearth Road rabble are L7-9 against a party of about L8, so the settled decision 'weaker enemies visibly flee and walking into them is an instant win' mostly disappears in M3 and entirely in the Act II open world. C's rabbleLevels = 2 (the brief's 'rabble never level up') must be adopted.
B (and C as written): running rules/migrate.js inside core/save.js's loadGame breaks the ARCHITECTURE.md rule that core imports nothing game-specific. Pass the migration in (A's pattern).
A: reading aethermoor.save.v1 whenever v2 is empty brings an erased M2 journey back after 'Start over'. It destroys nothing, but it surprises the player. Add B's migrated marker.

B: the scope is not buildable in one milestone by 8 agents who cannot run git: 21 maps, a script VM with battle and reload resume, a scheduled Tally-Wagon, dream fights, and real-time pack AI all in rules. It is the design most likely to ship half-finished.
B and C: adding scale:.5/back:true to heroForge (art/heroes.js) changes the battle hero rig the player approved. Isolate the walker rig, or gate the change with a snapshot diff.

C, needs a fix: with rabbleLevels = 2, variant holders of rabble families (Mags, Gorrow) escalate as rabble, because escalateSpawn reads the base family's tier and not the variant's. Hard relic-holder fights would become pushovers, or worse, a relic holder could be Routed with no pry-out.
C: the p95 < 8 ms frame gate in headless e2e will flake and block integration. Use 16 ms at 4x throttle.
B: Tamsin is written 'he/his', but the shipped prologue says 'Tamsin already has X over her shoulder' (newgame.js:292). The temper formula is misread (the code uses floor(temper/2), not ceil).

scores.notes: Best engineering base, and the claims I checked against the code hold. stats.js:60 does apply floor(temper/2). Tamsin is 'she' (newgame.js:292). core/save.js has the only storage key 'aethermoor.save.v1'. earnBrand really teleports to START and wipes `cleared`. The migration is injected into loadGame/importCode, which keeps core/ free of game logic as ARCHITECTURE requires. It is idempotent and fills missing fields on v2. It keeps `progress.node`. Real v1 fixtures (18) are generated from the M2 rules before anyone edits gauntlet.js, and a snapshot of the M2 spawn arrays protects the `id#i` grudge and echo keys. Roamers move on ticks in pure rules/world.js with their own RNG stream, so battles stay replayable and everything tests in node. A dedicated 16x24 walker rig leaves heroes.js/heroForge alone, so battle sprites are safe from parallel edits. The WP split is the most balanced (world engine vs flow/save vs maps vs data). It has concrete budgets, a p95 frame e2e at 4x throttle, and a road->world alias, and it keeps the M2 dist file. Weaknesses: (1) no party followers, so only the leader shows gear on the map; (2) the migration writes flags.done['briarmaw-den'] while its own test requires `done` to be deep-equal; (3) the spawnsFor memo key leaves out grudges and shattered state; (4) rabble still gain +6 levels per Waking, so the flee/instant-win promise mostly dies after Brand 1; (5) no skill checks with shown odds (brief section 10); (6) opening Mossway/Fawnrest before the Brand makes balance order-dependent, though the side-first/side-last sim modes cover it. The 3-piece Rotwarden and 13 maps are a realistic scope.

Richest world: 21 maps, 4 Keep interiors with a walkable reliquary, 3 Mosswatch floors plus an undercroft, 3 Heartroot floors, 10 Hearthfires with cold ones, the Pale Hart dream, First Seed return-or-keep, Unsmith letters, a Tally-Wagon on a day schedule. It has exactly 4 Relic-Bearer families, soft darkness, skill checks with odds and a Nearby DOM list, and its facts are accurate (the lore PNG really is 1536x1024). Tech-lead problems: (1) the camera k=floor(deviceWidth/240) gives about 17-19 tiles across on a 360px phone, so 16x24 walkers land near 21 CSS px and the gear becomes unreadable; (2) a script VM whose `progress.resume` continuation must survive battle, aftermath, a page reload and three separate owners, the riskiest piece of any design; (3) the overworld-art agent edits art/heroes.js heroForge (scale/back) while battle art and battle heroes depend on it; (4) WP-E owns the migration, core/save, the shell and 11 screens, which is a bottleneck, and the design never says how core/save calls rules/migrate without breaking layering; (5) inconsistencies: temper is quoted as ceil (the code uses floor), Tamsin is 'he' (the prologue says she), and earnBrand says 'except the one that granted it' while the table says Briarmaw re-arms as an Echo; (6) rules/foe.js, loot.js and ui/lib/items.js have no owner; (7) relic-bearer variants of rabble or veteran families get the wrong Omen count because escalateSpawn reads FOES[family].tier, not the variant's tier. Too much scope for one milestone of parallel agents.

Best player experience, with real brief fidelity: a four-hero conga line wearing real gear plus a 'showoff' when gear changes; hold-to-inspect grey card with Sighted stamp (brief section 1); a pre-fight card so you never blunder into a boss; dialogue that replaces the control deck in place; onboarding hints; 'Continue from the Gauntlet' with a carry-over card that writes nothing until you move; `.v2.bak` before New Game or import; integer device-pixel scale math (s=clamp(round(devicePx/192),2,8), about 11 tiles and 32x48 CSS walkers); an Atlas pin that slides along the route line. It also spots that rabble must stop leveling (TUNING.waking.rabbleLevels=2) or they never flee after Brand 1. Crownwalls make balance predictable, since all post-Brand content is always met at Waking 1. Tech-lead problems: (1) WP4 alone owns world, roam, script, migrate, gauntlet, battle, stats and party plus 5 test files, the critical-path bottleneck; (2) the Tamsin duel against the Warden alone needs a 1-hero battle layout that neither the engine, the UI nor the sim supports (flagged, with a fallback); (3) the same heroForge coupling and migration layering gap as B; (4) the same persisted script resume as B; (5) a long list of new settings, and the example card text ('you wake at the Milestone Fire') contradicts its own migration rule (Waking>0 goes to the Keep hall); (6) ui/lib/items.js has no owner even though the 1:1 temper change needs it.

best_ideas_to_graft: C: party followers (4 walkers stepping into the leader's old tiles) plus the gear 'showoff'. Build them on A's dedicated walker rig so every hero's gear shows on the map without touching heroForge.
C: TUNING.waking.rabbleLevels (for example 2; the brief says rabble 'never level up'), so rabble visibly flee and can be routed after Brand 1. Gate it with the Waking-1 sim.

C: a pre-fight card on blocks and lairs (level vs party, rated Easy/Fair/Hard/Deadly in words, Omens, Grudge title, the held relic's grey card, Fight / Not yet) and hold-450ms-to-inspect via cardPreview(item,{heldBy}) that stamps Sighted. This extends A's encounter sheet.

C + B save UX: 'Continue from the Gauntlet' with the carry-over card, and nothing written until the first move. Write `.v2.bak` before New Game or import. Add B's `aethermoor.v1.migrated` marker so 'Start over' does not silently re-import the M2 save. Keep A's injected migrate, its AETH2 prefix and its never-write-v1 rule.

C: integer device-pixel camera scale, s=clamp(round(devicePx/192),2,8), with one logical canvas and CSS pixelated scaling. That gives about 11 tiles across on a 360px phone, 32x48 CSS walkers and crisp pixels.
C: on phones, dialogue replaces the control deck in place (the advance button sits where A was), with a prompt line above the d-pad ('A · Talk to Captain Dael', and lock key ticks).

B/C: skill checks that show their odds (Garret's contest, exposing Vesper). Implement them as a `check` effect in A's dialogue data, rolled from rngState with a failure branch. Use no persisted script VM or `progress.resume`; derive post-fight quest state from flags as A does.
B: soft darkness (2-tile vision without a key) instead of a hard dark lock, and a cold-hearth lock type for extra Hearthfires (kindled = fast-travel point).
B/C: earnBrand pushes only Brands not already held (a rematch sets report.rematch). Briarmaw returns as an Echo rematch with no second Brand, instead of A's migration writing done['briarmaw-den'].

B/C: an optional hard area visible early at Waking 0 (Haskett, Lv 10, glinting across the millrace on the Hearth Road, fordable at once with Stillwater), plus the walkable reliquary with a lit pedestal per claimed relic.
B: exactly 4 Relic-Bearer families to match the brief (e.g. gloamwing, palehart), and the Nearby DOM-button list for keyboard and screen-reader play.
B/C: also write dist/aethermoor-m3.html so the M2 download is never overwritten (alongside A's dist/aethermoor-m2.html copy).
C: the Atlas 'you are here' pin interpolated along each route's atlas line, and a travel list under the map on phones.
Fallback if Gate-3 balance misses under A's open pre-Brand world: adopt B/C crownwalls, so all post-Brand leads are met only at Waking 1.
fatal_flaws: A: migrate() writes flags.done['briarmaw-den']=true for Brand holders, but A's own WP-B test requires `done` to stay deep-equal, so Gate 1 fails as written. Derive Briarmaw's 'beaten' state from progress.brands instead of mutating done.

A: 'spawnsFor is memoised per (encounter, waking, set of claimed relics)' leaves out grudges and shattered inventory, so after a flee or wipe the map and sheet would show stale Grudge titles and Omens. Key the memo on the game object, or include grudges and shattered state.
A: with no party followers (its cut #1), only the leader's gear is visible on the map. That misses the brief's 'see it on your sprite ... on the map' for the other three heroes.

B: the camera scale k=floor(deviceWidth/240) gives about 17-19 tiles across on a 360px phone. 16x24 walkers render at about 21 CSS px and the gear on them can't be read, which defeats the core promise.

B/C: a script continuation `progress.resume={script,pc,win,lose}` persisted through battle, aftermath and a page reload, with three owners (script rules, world screen, aftermath). This is the highest-risk integration and needs its own e2e test. A derives quest state from flags and needs none.

B/C: rules/migrate.js must be called from core/save.js loadGame/importCode. A direct import breaks ARCHITECTURE's 'core imports nothing game-specific' rule. Inject it from the shell (A's loadGame(migrate) / importCode(code, migrate)).

B/C: the overworld-art agent adds scale/back to art/heroes.js heroForge while the battle-art agent's humanoid foes (foes.js imports heroForge) and the shipped battle heroes depend on it. That invites regressions in battle sprites across parallel agents; A's separate walker rig avoids it.

C: Tamsin fights the Warden alone, but createBattle callers, the battle UI layout, the sim and party.active all assume 4 heroes, and there is no 1-hero layout. Use Tamsin plus cadets against the full party (C's own cut 4) or A/B's party-vs-Tamsin.
C: WP4 (world, roam, script, migrate, gauntlet, battle, stats, party and 5 test files) is one agent on the critical path. B's WP-E (save, migrate, shell, 11 screens) is the same kind of bottleneck.

All: rules/foe.js escalateSpawn and addOmens read FOES[spawn.family].tier, not familyOf(spawn).tier. Relic-bearer variants of rabble or veteran families (B/C's Mags, Hollis, Haskett, Corra...) get the wrong Omen count at each Waking. Use familyOf there.

All: migration must keep the Waking, so M2 players who looped Briarmaw to Waking 2 meet the Rotwarden at about L18-20. Only A makes a Waking-2 fixture. The balance sim must include looper fixtures, or Champions need a party-level clamp, or the player's own save could hit a wall.

scores.notes: The strongest engineering of the three and the most faithful geography. Every map carries its lore-map coordinate and the connections read correctly: Thornhollow, then west to the Mossway and Mosswatch, north to Eldergrove, and on to Fawnrest by several routes. Every lock really has two keys, and there are no thorn-walls without one. The future-region plumbing is the best: a REGIONS table, 5 sealed exits, and a second way into both Gloomfen (the Fen Stair toward Willowmurk) and Ironspire (the Highfold Path, with a bell hinting at Peak's Veil), which matches the brief's 'at least two ways in'. The Ladder shows Act II silhouettes, the Hearth Clock shows 'Brands x/8', and 'The way opens in the next chapter' appears after act1-complete. Named holders reuse names already in foes.js (Mother Brisk, Hobb Two-Knives, Ledger-Maud, Quill, Hollis Fairweight). Tamsin is correctly 'she'. The save plan is the best engineered: fixtures are frozen from the M2 rules before anything changes, migrate is injected into core/save.js, the v1 key is never written, and there is an Export M2 backup button. Fidelity misses: no Unsmith letters (brief §3), no walkable Reliquary with pedestals (§5), no dialogue skill checks with odds (§10), no Alondra dream of four Sleepers, and Temper does not visibly brighten. Its 'optional hard area visible early' is weak: the Smugglers' Hollow sits in the Mossway, not in sight of the early road. The Domain keys Attunement 9 and 10 go past the brief's 'Domains up to 7' for M3. Act I opens at Thornhollow, before any Brand, so it is less guided than the brief's Act I. Internal slips: the migration sets done['briarmaw-den'] even though its own test says `done` is copied byte for byte, and it calls ANCHOR() with a different signature from the one §4.1 defines. The lockstep roamers are very testable but feel less alive than real-time packs.

The richest world and the richest use of the lore map. Vesper's miracle sap is the pilgrims' 'miraculous healing' rumour. The feral druids perform their rites at the Grove-Heart. The Dreaming Stone and Pale Hart carry the prophetic dreams. The Keep has refugees. Hollis's signals and ledger ('ichor to the Fen buyer') seed Gloomfen. Hilda reads Harrow's mark on the mask. There are Unsmith letters after each Brand, reliquary pedestals with riddles, and skill checks that show their odds. The sealed-exit text names the brief's two ways into each region (dune-glass or the caravans, the rockslide or Stormwatch's writ, Blackwater), and Poacher's Holm is an optional hard fight you can see from the road. Problems: Tamsin is 'he/his' in the boss section, but the shipped prologue says 'her' (newgame.js:292). The camera `k=floor(deviceWidth/240)` shows 15–19 tiles across, so a 16×24 walker is about 21×32 CSS px on a 360 px phone. That is too small to read the gear, which is the brief's core 'see it on your sprite' hook. The geography is odd in one place: Smugglers' Run branches east off the Hearth Road and then leads north to Mossfall, which sits west of Thornhollow. The crownwalls are thorn walls with no key other than a Brand. At 21 maps with a script VM that resumes after a battle, it outgrows the 1.5–2 h slice. It deletes progress.node, but aftermath.js:58 and title.js:25 still read ENCOUNTERS[game.progress.node]. It misquotes temper as ceil; the code uses floor. WP-E is overloaded. It adds a v1-migrated marker, a good touch.

The best phone-first experience of the brief. Its scale maths (s=6 at DPR 3, an 11-tile view) makes a walker 32×48 CSS px, so helms and weapons read. Dialogue takes over the control deck so your thumb never moves. Every lair and block has a pre-fight card rated Easy/Fair/Hard/Deadly. Holding a lair for 450 ms shows the greyed card and marks it Sighted, as the brief asks, with an e2e test. A 'showoff' plays when gear changes, and about 10 lines react to what you wear ('The world notices'). Temper visibly brightens the metal, as the brief says. `rabbleLevels=2` honours 'rabble never level up', so rabble really flee after Brand 1. On the Atlas, 'you are here' slides along each map's line on the lore map, and the lore-map coordinates are used faithfully. Tamsin is 'she'. It mirrors the brief's guided-then-open shape as a rehearsal for Act II: guided to Briarmaw, then three leads in any order that each arm you against the Rotwarden. Poacher's Holm is a hard area you can see early. Saves are the gentlest: the v1 key is read-only and never written, a .v2.bak is taken before New Game or import, and 'Continue from the Gauntlet' shows a carry-over card and writes nothing until you move. Weaknesses: the crownwall is the same single-key thorn gate as B's. WP4 owns world, roam, script, migrate, gauntlet, battle, stats and party, which is a critical-path bottleneck. Its migration sends every Waking>0 save to the Keep, even a player mid-way through a second M2 run, and the sample card says 'you wake at the Milestone Fire', which contradicts that. The Unsmith letter comes only after Brand 2, and there is no Harrow hook. The solo Tamsin duel needs a one-hero battle layout; a fallback is listed.

best_ideas_to_graft: From A, split C's overloaded WP4: rules/world.js becomes a pure lockstep API (move, interact and tick return events; plus enterMap and findPath), with its own walk RNG seeded 'roam:'+seed+':'+map+':'+visits that never touches game.rngState. WP4 keeps flow, migrate, story and the battle tweaks. Movement, locks, roamers and 'can Act I be finished' then all test in node.

From A, run tools/make-v1-fixtures.mjs against the unmodified M2 gauntlet.js before any agent touches rules/ (the agents cannot use git). Freeze one save at each of the 14 nodes, one after the Brand, one at Waking 2 with duplicate 'brand-of-briars', one with grudges and one with a shattered Thornsplitter. Deep-equal every kept field.

From A, inject the migration into core/save.js as loadGame(migrate) and importCode(code, migrate), so core stays free of game logic. Add an 'Export M2 backup (AETH1)' button that reads the untouched v1 key.

From B, add an aethermoor.v1.migrated marker so that erasing or replacing the M3 save never resurrects the Gauntlet save, and offer 'Restore my M2 save' in Settings. Keep C's .v2.bak and B/C's separate dist/aethermoor-m3.html so neither the M2 save nor the M2 download is overwritten.

From A, use five sealed exits so Gloomfen and Ironspire each already show two ways in: the Keep SW gate plus the Mossfall Fen Stair toward Willowmurk, and the Keep E gate plus Fawnrest's Highfold Path with a bell toward Peak's Veil. Add a data/world.js REGIONS table (act, lore centre, entry exits, Brand ids) and the line 'The way opens in the next chapter' after act1-complete. Use B's exit text, which names the brief's second key for each region: dune-glass or the Sandspire caravans, the rockslide or Stormwatch's writ, Blackwater or Willowmurk.

From A, give the Ladder three Act II silhouettes: a glass scorpion, the Lantern Mother and the missing smith. Name the Verdant holders from the lists already in foes.js (Hollis Fairweight, Dun the Counter, Ledger-Maud, Quill, Mother Brisk, Hobb Two-Knives).

From A, per-map 'v1:<encounterId>' anchors with a walkability test. Add a reachability test that uses only the keys guaranteed at each point, including the shattered-Thornsplitter path (Warden L5, Physical 3).

From B, an Unsmith letter after every Brand (brief §3), including Brand 1. Hilda reads the Ichor Mask's maker's mark (the Harrow hook). Hollis's tally-sealed ledger reads 'ichor, south, to the Fen buyer' (the Gloomfen hook).

From B, the data test checks each die against `v.tier || f.tier`. Also make escalateSpawn and the tier checks in startBattle read the variant's tier through familyOf, so relic-bearer variants of veteran families get the right Omen count.

Fix the crownwall so it stops competing with the Thornsplitter. Draw it as Briarmaw's living crown-growth, visibly unlike a thornwall. Cutting it with the Thornsplitter or Physical 3 plays a line: 'The hatchet bounces. These grew from Briarmaw's crown.' The Journal calls it a story seal, not a lock. Borrow the lore map's detail that Thornhollow's thorn walls regrow overnight for flavour.

Count unique Brands for the Hearth Clock and the end card, because M2 saves can carry duplicate 'brand-of-briars'. Add a Waking-2 looper mode to the sim, since that player meets the second half at +12 levels.
fatal_flaws: B and C, two keys per lock: the crownwalls are thorn walls that only a Brand opens. The Thornsplitter cannot cut them and no Domain key works, which breaks the player's settled 'two keys for every lock' unless they are re-skinned and clearly presented as a story seal.

B, phone readability: the camera `k=floor(deviceWidth/240)` gives 15–19 tiles across, so a 16×24 walker is about 21×32 CSS px on a 360 px phone. Gear on the sprite, the brief's core hook, becomes unreadable. Use C's scale maths (s = clamp(round(devicePx/192), 2, 8)).

B and C delete progress.node, but aftermath.js:58 and title.js:25 still read ENCOUNTERS[game.progress.node]. The same package must update those screens, or migrated saves break on the aftermath or title screen. Keeping node verbatim and never reading it, as A does, is safer.

A: the migration writes done['briarmaw-den'] while its preservation test requires `done` to deep-equal the v1 save, so its own gate fails. The migration also calls ANCHOR() with a different signature from §4.1. Pick one (put the Briarmaw state in a new flag) before building.

All three: M2 let players re-beat Briarmaw, so real v1 saves can hold brands ['brand-of-briars','brand-of-briars'] and Waking 2. The Hearth Clock must count unique Brands. The migration must keep the Waking, as required, and the balance pass must cover post-Brand content at +12 levels, or those players hit a wall at the Rotwarden.

C: WP4 owns world, roam, script, migrate, gauntlet, battle, stats and party. With 6–8 parallel agents that is one critical-path owner for most of the rules, and it has to be split for the plan to parallelise.
B: 21 maps plus a script VM whose continuation survives a battle and a reload is more than the 1.5–2 h slice, and the biggest schedule risk of the three.
